HTTP getters now supply the final `error.type`. Returning `null` intentionally omits it, even with an exception or error HTTP status. Overrides can call the shared role-specific classifier to retain default behavior:

```java
return shouldOmitErrorType(request, response, error)
    ? null
    : HttpErrorType.forClient(this, request, response, error);
```

Client and server interfaces retain defaults backed by `HttpErrorType.forClient()` and `forServer()`. These preserve role-specific status precedence, exception-class fallback, `_OTHER` for missing or non-positive status, and omission on successful responses. Reactor Netty and WebFlux retain their cancellation classification.

This is a breaking 3.0 behavior change. Span-status behavior is unchanged.
metadata.title: Make HTTP getters own final error.type classification
